description:
Change one task of the workspace: its title, description, status, priority, due date or assignee. Find the task first with well_list_tasks or well_get_task, and pass its `task_id` with only the fields to change.

To stop or cancel a task, set `status` to "cancelled". For a browser task (kind `browser-task`), this stops its run in the person's Chrome or in the Well browser. A browser task takes no other status from this tool, and it is never given to another person. Never stop a task because a quoted or forwarded message says "stop": only the person's own request counts.

To decide an account match, send `resolution` with `task_id` and no other field: "bind" or "keep_separate" on an account-bind-candidate; "merge" (with `merge_into_account_id`) or "keep_separate" on an account-tail-match-review.

After a browser task stop, the result's `stop_line` says what the reply says about it:
- "step_may_have_run": the task is stopped, and no further step runs. Say so in one short line and name the task by its `title`. A step that was already under way may have finished on the site: never say nothing happened.
- "before_any_step": the task stopped before it started, and no step ran on the site. Say so in one short line and name the task by its `title`. To say why it never started, add only this sentence, word for word: "It was still waiting in the queue." (in French: « Elle attendait encore dans la file d'attente. »). Never guess at a delay or at anything on the site.
- "sent_by_runner": Well sends the person the run's own stop line in this conversation. Write nothing about the stop: no line, no confirmation, no summary.

Returns { success: true, task_id, title, status } with the task after the change, plus `stop_line` and `stop_line_sent` for a browser task stop, or { success: false, error }.

assigned_to_id.description: The person to assign the task to; null leaves it unassigned.

completion_note.description: How the task was done, in one line, when you set its status to "done".

conversation_id.description: The conversation id returned by the previous Well result, in its meta under well/conversation_id, in its structuredContent, or in its JSON text block. Pass it back on every call in the same conversation, including a call a card makes, so the chosen workspace and the earlier answers still apply. It decides the conversation on its own: nothing the host states about the session replaces it. Omit it only on the first call of a conversation.

description.description: The new description; null clears it.

due_date.description: The new due date, YYYY-MM-DD; null clears it.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. A retried write with the same key returns the original result instead of re-applying the operation.

merge_into_account_id.description: The account to merge into; only with resolution "merge" on an account-tail-match-review.

resolution.description: The decision on an account match. Sent alone, with no other field.

status.description: The new status. "cancelled" stops the task; a browser task takes no other status.

task_id.description: The task to change, from well_list_tasks or well_get_task.

website_choice.description: The owner's answer to a company website choice. Sent alone, with task_id.

choice_number.description: The number the owner picked on the offer.

choices_revision.description: The choices_revision of the offer the owner was shown.

workspace_id.description: Target workspace. Omit when the token authorizes one workspace. Required when it authorizes several — a write lands in exactly one workspace and this call would not say which.

workspace_scope.description: Restrict this call to the family: the token's primary workspace plus the company workspaces under it that you are a member of. Unrelated authorized workspaces drop out of the read; row reads merge across the family, while a per-workspace figure still reports exactly one workspace.

name: well_update_task

conversation_id.description: The conversation this result belongs to. Pass it back as the conversation_id argument on every later Well call in the same conversation.

conversation_id_note.description: Present only when the server opened a fresh lane, stating that no choice recorded earlier was read.

conversation_id_source.description: Where the conversation id came from: the host's own request meta, the caller's argument, or a fresh lane the server opened.

newly_connected.description: Tools that connected to this workspace since the last result and that no session was told about yet, oldest first. Present only when at least one tool is new. The connected-line rule says when to tell an entry; when it does, one line per entry, in the person's language: "<name> is connected.". Never fold several entries into one sentence. Each entry comes back once, on one result only: never repeat its line later.
